2027-03-24.title: Wednesday of Holy Week
readings: I did not hide my face from insult and spitting (Third Song of the Servant)
Lord, in your great love, answer me
The Son of Man goes as it is written of him, but woe to that one by whom the Son of Man is betrayed
2027-03-24.alt: Holy Week. Lent continues until the evening Mass of the Lord's Supper on Thursday. No Gloria, no Alleluia. Liturgical colour: violet. Traditionally called Spy Wednesday, from the bargain of Judas. This is the last full day of Lent; the Easter Triduum begins tomorrow evening. Some parishes keep Tenebrae tonight.
2027-03-24.verse: The Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame.
theo: The third Song of the Servant is the song of a disciple. “The Lord GOD has given me the tongue of a teacher, that I may know how to sustain the weary with a word. Morning by morning he wakens, wakens my ear to listen as those who are taught.” Before the Servant speaks, he listens; every morning he lets God open his ear. Because he listens, he does not turn back when suffering comes: “I gave my back to those who struck me, and my cheeks to those who pulled out the beard; I did not hide my face from insult and spitting.” His strength is not hardness but trust: “The Lord GOD helps me… therefore I have set my face like flint.” We heard this same reading on Palm Sunday; today it prepares us for the night of Thursday and the day of Friday, when Jesus will be struck, mocked and spat upon, and will not hide his face. The Psalm is the cry of the righteous sufferer whom even his own family treats as a stranger: “It is zeal for your house that has consumed me… for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.” The Gospels saw this psalm fulfilled on Calvary (John 2:17; 19:28–29).

The Gospel tells the bargain. Judas goes to the chief priests and asks: “What will you give me if I betray him to you?” They pay him thirty pieces of silver. That was the price of a slave in the Law (Exodus 21:32), and the “lordly price” at which the shepherd of Zechariah was valued (Zechariah 11:12–13). From this bargain the day takes its old name in English, Spy Wednesday. Then the scene moves to preparation: “Where do you want us to make the preparations for you to eat the Passover?” Jesus is not a victim caught by surprise. He says: “My time is near; I will keep the Passover at your house with my disciples.” He walks freely into his hour.

At table he says: “Truly I tell you, one of you will betray me.” And each disciple asks, “Surely not I, Lord?” That is the right question for us too. None of the Eleven was sure of himself; each knew that his heart could fail. Judas also asks, but notice the difference: the others say “Lord”; he says “Rabbi”, teacher. Jesus answers, “You have said so,” leaving the door open even now. The words of Jesus about Judas are solemn: “woe to that one by whom the Son of Man is betrayed!” They are not a curse but a lament, the grief of a friend. The Church does not pretend to know the final state of any soul; she knows that despair was Judas's last and greatest tragedy, and that no betrayal is greater than the mercy of Christ. On this last day before the Triduum, let us ask with the apostles, “Surely not I, Lord?”, and then run to the One who is about to give his life for betrayers, deniers and deserters, which is to say, for all of us.
conn: Isaiah 50:4–9 (the Lectionary stops at 9a). The Servant is first a disciple, one who listens “as those who are taught.” The Song is read on Palm Sunday and again today.
The compensation for a slave gored by an ox (Exodus 21:32). Matthew sees Zechariah's “thirty shekels of silver” fulfilled (Matthew 27:9–10).
An old English name for this day, after Judas, who from this day watched for an opportunity to hand Jesus over. In some lands the day is still marked by Tenebrae.
The first day of Unleavened Bread.
The Passover lamb was sacrificed on the afternoon of 14 Nisan and eaten that evening; for seven days no leaven was eaten (Exodus 12:15–20).
In Matthew the faithful disciples call Jesus “Lord”; only Judas calls him “Rabbi” at the Supper and in Gethsemane (Matthew 26:25, 49).
Latin for darkness. A service of psalms and lamentations in which candles are put out one by one until the church is dark; a loud noise at the end recalls the earthquake at the death of Christ.
fathers: Judas, more wicked than all, did not repent and seek pardon; had he not hastened to the noose, he could have obtained mercy. His despair, not only his betrayal, was his ruin.
See the gentleness of the Lord: even at the table he did not name the traitor before all, but gave him room to repent. He washed his feet and shared his bread, and still Judas did not turn back.
outline: Ask: what is a friendship worth? What would make someone sell it?
Morning by morning he wakens my ear.
He did not hide his face from insult.
The humble question of the disciple.
“The Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced.”
live: Tomorrow morning, before your phone, read the Gospel of the day in silence for ten minutes.
Ask: for what do I betray Jesus? Money, comfort, the opinion of others? Name it and give it up for the Triduum.
Prepare your home and your heart for the Triduum: clean, decide the family's times, and plan to keep Good Friday's fast.
2027-03-24.prayer: Lord Jesus, Servant who listened morning by morning, you set your face like flint and did not hide it from insult and spitting. You were sold for thirty pieces of silver by a friend. Keep us from selling you for any price. Let us ask humbly, Surely not I, Lord?, and run to your mercy. Bring us with you into these holy days. Amen.
altar: The one who was sold for thirty pieces of silver gives himself to us freely at the altar. What Judas sold, the Church receives as pure gift.

quick: The Servant listens to God every morning and does not turn back from suffering.
Judas sells Jesus for thirty pieces of silver.
Each disciple asks, Surely not I, Lord? We ask it too, and trust his mercy.
2027-03-24.action: Prepare your home and heart for the Triduum: confession, family timetable, and the Good Friday fast.
2027-03-24.question: For what price am I tempted to sell my friendship with Jesus?

family.explain: Judas was one of Jesus' friends, but he sold Jesus for thirty silver coins. That was a very sad thing. Jesus still loved him. Jesus is our best friend, and we never want to trade him for anything.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always stay close to Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do to get our home ready for Holy Thursday, Good Friday and Easter?”

illus: A businessman in Kochi was offered a large contract if he would sign false accounts. It was Holy Week. On Wednesday evening he heard the Gospel: “What will you give me if I betray him to you?” He went home and told his wife he could not sign. They lost the contract and had a hard year. Years later he said to his son: the price was very high, but it was much less than thirty pieces of silver. I would have sold my Lord and my peace.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were sold for thirty pieces of silver and you did not turn back. Open our ears morning by morning and keep us faithful. Amen.
share: Morning by morning he wakens my ear (Isaiah 50:4). Do I begin my day by listening to God?
What will you give me if I betray him? (Matthew 26:15). For what do I sell my faith?
Surely not I, Lord? (Matthew 26:22). Do I ask this question humbly, or do I trust myself too much?
pm.resp: Lord, in your great love, answer me.
interc: For all who are tempted to betray a friend, a spouse or their conscience for money.
For those who suffer insult and violence for doing what is right.
For the despairing, that they may find the mercy Judas refused.
For all who prepare the Holy Week liturgies in our parish.
For our group, that we may enter the Triduum with listening hearts.
pm.close: Father, your Son set his face like flint to do your will. Help us to follow him faithfully through these holy days. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today the Servant tells us his secret: the Lord GOD has given me the tongue of a teacher, that I may know how to sustain the weary with a word. Morning by morning he wakens, wakens my ear to listen as those who are taught (Isaiah 50:4). Before he speaks, he listens. And because he listens, he does not turn back: I did not hide my face from insult and spitting (Isaiah 50:6).

In the Gospel Judas goes to the chief priests and asks: what will you give me if I betray him to you? They paid him thirty pieces of silver (Matthew 26:15). The price of a slave. The Son of God, valued at thirty coins.

At the table Jesus says: one of you will betray me. And each disciple asks: surely not I, Lord? (Matthew 26:22). They do not point at each other. Each looks into his own heart. That is the question for us on this last day before the Triduum. For what price would I sell Jesus? For money? For comfort? For the approval of others?

But remember: Jesus did not curse Judas; he grieved over him and even at the table left the door open. No sin is bigger than his mercy. Tomorrow evening the Triduum begins. Let us come to it as the Servant did, with a listening ear and a face set like flint, trusting that the Lord GOD helps us. Amen.
kids: Children, Judas sold Jesus for thirty silver coins. How sad! Jesus is worth more than all the money and toys in the world. Let us tell Jesus today: you are my best friend, and I will never trade you for anything!

intro: Theme: “The Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced.”
The listening Servant, the face like flint, the thirty pieces of silver and the humble question of the disciple.

q: The Lord GOD has given me the tongue of a teacher, that I may know how to sustain the weary with a word.

“Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
points.apply: Begin each day of the Triduum with ten minutes of silent listening to the Word.

sub: He did not hide his face.
q: The Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame;

looking to Jesus the pioneer and perfecter of our faith, who for the sake of the joy that was set before him endured the cross, disregarding its shame, and has taken his seat at the right hand of the throne of God.
points.apply: When you are insulted this week, keep silence and pray for the one who insulted you.

sub: For what do I sell him?
q: So they weighed out as my wages thirty shekels of silver.
“What will you give me if I betray him to you?” They paid him thirty pieces of silver.
points.apply: Name the price for which you are tempted to betray Jesus, and renounce it in confession.

q: Insults have broken my heart, so that I am in despair. I looked for pity, but there was none; and for comforters, but I found none.
And they became greatly distressed and began to say to him one after another, “Surely not I, Lord?”
points.apply: Enter the Triduum in humility: ask Jesus to keep you faithful, and trust his mercy if you fall.

concl: The Servant listens, suffers and trusts; he does not turn back.
Judas sold him; we ask humbly, Surely not I, Lord?, and run to his mercy.
